title: pii
text:
Personal information, often called PII, is text that identifies a person or opens one of their accounts: an email address, a phone number, a card or bank account number, a national identity number such as a UK National Insurance number or an Indian Aadhaar number, a street address, a date of birth, an API key or password. The detector is a separate package, rahasya. It works with patterns and checksums rather than a model. A card number has to pass the Luhn check and an NHS number its mod-11 check, so the detector gives the same answer every time and downloads nothing. On a held-out test set of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm (evals/RESULTS.md, section 3).
Names are the gap. No pattern describes a name, so name detection is a second pass, and it finds only a name that follows a title such as Mr, Dr or Prof: “Dr Charles Babbage” is found, “Ada Lovelace” on her own is not. The pass runs when a document is added (except on code, where identifiers are not names) and by default in ask; Vault.pii and gated run it only with ner=True. When a document holds personal information the detector cannot see, a person marks it, as below.
This page is the half of the work that needs a vault: the marks a person sets, the privacy level of each document, the table of findings, and gated, which applies a policy to what search and reading return. What ask and the other model calls send to a model is on ask.

title: pii
section: Checking a document, and gating retrieval
text:
Checking a document, and gating retrieval
Vault.pii(ref) answers for one whole document: whether it holds personal information, which kinds, and whether a person’s mark overrides the detector. detected is the detector’s own verdict and override is the mark. mark_pii marks a document as personal when the detector finds nothing, for example a letter that names people without titles. mark_not_pii clears a false alarm, such as your own invoice, and only a person may set it (see the next section). pii_ctx runs the detector over every section of an assembled context, the result of context, which is what ask decides on.
Retrieval is the other half. search, sections, context, read, document, toc, doc_context and federate all take pii=, which says what happens to a row that holds personal information:







pii=
the row’s text becomes




off, the default in Python and the CLI
the stored text; nothing is checked


redact
the stored text with each recognised identifier replaced by its kind, as in [EMAIL]


refuse
a placeholder such as [withheld: personal information (card, email)]



Under redact and refuse the row stays in the results, its title and breadcrumb are masked rather than removed, and a pii key names the kinds found, so a caller can still say why something was held back. Three cases follow from the levels below. A Local only document is withheld under redact as well as refuse, and so are its title, breadcrumb and source. A document that is private only because of a mark or the shelf’s floor, with nothing the detector recognises, passes through redact unchanged, because there is nothing to mask; use refuse when that matters. A document a person cleared with mark_not_pii comes back untouched, unless the shelf’s floor is above Open.
The MCP server hands its results to a model the vault does not run, so there every tool defaults to redact, and every result is gated whatever the tool, including ask’s. A client may ask for refuse. It may not ask for off.

title: pii
section: Learned detectors were measured and not shipped
text:
Learned detectors were measured and not shipped
Two learned PII models, an ONNX build and a TFLite build, were tried against the patterns. Both were worse on precision and on recall, and about 200 times slower, so the shipped detector is the patterns alone. The model code stays in evals/backends.py, evals/pii_model.py reruns the comparison, and evals/RESULTS.md has the numbers.

title: pii
text:
Privacy levels and findings
Every document has one of three privacy levels. The level decides what this package’s own model calls may send to a model that runs somewhere other than this machine, called a hosted model below.



level
how a document gets it
what a hosted model may be sent




Open (open)
nothing personal found, or a person cleared it
the text as it is


Personal (personal)
the detector found an identifier, or someone marked it
it depends on the policy: masked text, nothing, or with allow=True the whole text (see ask)


Local only (local)
someone set it with set_level, or its type is sensitive
nothing; only a model on this machine reads it



The sensitive types come from varga: passport, ID card, bank statement, payslip, tax return and clinical record. These rules cover what vishalakshi sends to models. In Python and the CLI they do not stop retrieval: read or search with the default pii='off' still returns a Local only document’s text to whoever called it. The MCP server defaults to redact, which withholds it.
level(ref) works a document’s level out in three steps. A mark set with mark_pii, mark_not_pii or set_level, if there is one, decides. Otherwise the level is the higher of the type’s level and the findings’ level, where any identifier found in its text or its title makes it Personal. Finally the result is raised to the shelf’s floor. The floor is a level no document on the shelf can go below, set with set_floor. A shelf for medical records can have a floor of Local only, so a new document there is protected before anything has been detected in it. level(ref, page=n) gives one page’s level from that page’s findings; a page with no text takes the whole document’s level.
Raising a level is always allowed. Lowering one is not. set_level to a lower level, removing a mark, mark_not_pii, reject_pii, reset_pii and lowering a floor all take by= and raise PermissionError unless by='person'. The default is 'person', so a person’s own code passes nothing, and an agent passes its own name. The MCP server does not offer by, so a model client cannot claim to be a person, and it cannot turn the retrieval gate off with pii='off' either.
When a document is added, scan_pii scans each page and files every identifier in the pii_findings table as a finding: its kind, its page, its start and end offsets in the page text, and a fingerprint. The fingerprint is a 16-character hash of the kind and the value with spacing, dashes and case removed, so ADA@example.com and ada@example.com, or 4111-1111-1111-1111 and 4111 1111 1111 1111, give the same fingerprint. The table does not hold the value. The value is still in the document’s text, which the vault keeps as it was read, and the hash has no secret key, so a short value such as a date of birth could be recovered by hashing every possible one. Treat the findings table as exactly as private as the vault file. findings lists them, each with a masked preview such as a••@e••••••.com taken from the current page text.
A person can give a verdict on a finding. accept_pii confirms it is personal, which an agent may also do, since it can only raise a level. reject_pii says it is not, and the level falls if nothing else holds it up. reset_pii takes a verdict back. A verdict is stored against the fingerprint, so it covers every occurrence of the same value in the document and it survives the page being read again: the new findings get new ids and keep the old verdict. A finding id from before the re-read comes back as stale.

Retrieval defaults are litesearch’s. Reach for:

v.shelf(name) to keep two collections apart, so a large one does not crowd a small one out of the rankings

v.mark_noisy(doc_id, reason='site furniture')
v.mark_pii(doc_id, reason='address book'); v.mark_not_pii(doc_id, reason='my own invoice')

connect(), which needs a model, builds the typed entity graph (LLM refers_to/defines edges) and the topic nodes; graph_search walks it, map / topic_tree read topics. Run connect() after a batch of ingests.

forget, drop_shelf, unwatch and pause are not in allow; call them yourself when you mean to.
This page is a pyskill: a cheat sheet an agent loads with read_skill. The markdown cell above is exported as the module’s docstring, and list_pyskills() reads it without importing the module, taking the first paragraph as the summary. allow registers the vault methods a sandboxed agent may call, READ and WRITE: everything that reads the vault or adds to it. Deleting (forget, drop_shelf) and stopping watches (unwatch, pause) are left out, so an agent cannot do them.

title: read
text:
Many PDFs carry a text layer, the text you can select and copy. When the PDF was made from a digital document that layer is exact and costs nothing to read. A scanned PDF has no text layer, or one made by OCR (optical character recognition) that may be poor. Old books in Indian scripts are often worse: many were set in legacy fonts whose text layer reads as Latin gibberish, or splits akṣaras, the letter clusters of Devanagari, apart. A vision model, one that reads images, can read such a page from its picture, but it costs time or money for every page and makes mistakes of its own.
read_doc decides page by page, and parse sets the route:
model is any id Urai knows, local or hosted, such as claude/sonnet or gemini/gemini-2.5-flash; None means $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL. There are two ways in. The function read_doc(path) reads one file and returns its pages, with no vault involved. Vault.read_doc(src) reads a file, or every PDF and image under a folder, into the vault: each file becomes one document, and each page’s text, route and flags are kept as numbered versions, so reading a page again never loses an earlier reading.

title: read
text:
Prompts
A vision model is told what to return by a reading prompt. PRESETS holds four. Each asks for the page as JSON: a list of items in reading order, where an item is a heading, a paragraph of prose, a verse, a table, a note or a colophon (the line that closes a chapter in an Indian text), with its text exactly as printed and any number printed with it. Once read, these items are called blocks. generic suits any printed page. sanskrit and tamil name the letters that old prints in those scripts make easy to misread, and sanskrit also tells the model to leave out translation and commentary. tables reads tables as rows of cells.
Every preset also asks for a box per item: the region it covers, as [x0, y0, x1, y1] in fractions of the page’s width and height measured from the top left, so an app can crop the block out of the page image or highlight it.
reading_prompt fills a preset in with the document’s title, its script (Devanagari unless you say otherwise) and a hint, a sentence about this particular book, such as how it numbers its verses or what to skip. A preset that is not one of the four names is used as the whole prompt. If it contains {of}, {title}, {script} or {hint} they are filled in, and a prompt whose JSON braces are not doubled is sent unchanged.


source

reading_prompt
def reading_prompt(
    name:str='generic', title:str='', script:str='', hint:str=''
)->str:
Fill in the reading prompt name with the title, script and hint, or use name itself as the prompt when it is not a preset.



assert 'Gita' in reading_prompt('sanskrit', 'Gita') and 'ष look like प' in reading_prompt('sanskrit')
assert 'Tamil' in reading_prompt('tamil')
assert all('"box": [x0, y0, x1, y1]' in reading_prompt(k) and 'leave it out' in reading_prompt(k) for k in PRESETS)
test_eq(reading_prompt('Read it: {hint}', hint='x'), 'Read it: x')
test_eq(reading_prompt('A {script} page of {title}. {{"items": []}} {hint}', 'Gita', 'Tamil'), 'A Tamil page of Gita. {"items": []} ')
test_eq(reading_prompt('Return {"items": []} only.', 'Gita'), 'Return {"items": []} only.')   # no template: as it is

title: read
text:
Pages as images
A model is sent a picture of the page. render draws one page of a PDF as a PNG at dpi (200 by default). Some hosted models refuse large images, so when the PNG is over max_bytes (3 MB) render returns a JPEG whose long side fits max_px (3,000 pixels) instead, and fit does the same for an image file. Two cuts help with hard pages. halves splits a landscape image, usually a scan of two facing pages (a spread), into its left and right pages. page_strips cuts a tall page into overlapping horizontal strips, so the model sees worn or small type at a larger scale.

page_strips
def page_strips(
    img:bytes, k:int, over:float=0.06
)->list:
Cut img into k horizontal strips, top to bottom, each overlapping the next by over of the page height.

def halves(
    img:bytes
)->list:
Split a landscape page image, taken to be a two-page spread, into its left and right halves, and return any other image as it is.

fit
def fit(
    img:bytes, max_px:int=3000, max_bytes:int=3000000

Return img unchanged when it is within max_bytes, else as a JPEG whose long side fits max_px.

title: read
text:
Checks
flags lists what looks wrong with a page’s text. It is how parse='auto' decides that a text layer cannot be trusted.







flag
meaning




thin
fewer than min_chars (20) letters, as on a scanned page


replacement
the Unicode replacement character, which marks text that failed to decode


legacy
more than 5 Latin-1 or typographic characters per 100 letters, which is how a legacy Devanagari font’s text layer reads


split
a line that starts with a vowel sign or virāma, a piece of an akṣara cut off from the rest


akshara
an akṣara that cannot be written, such as a virāma followed by a vowel sign


foreign
Greek or Cyrillic letters next to Devanagari



disagree(a, b) measures how far two readings of the same text differ: the letter edits between them divided by the letters in the longer one. Spaces, digits, daṇḍas and punctuation are ignored and vowel signs count. A value of 0.1 or more is worth a look.


source

disagree
def disagree(
    a:str, b:str
)->float | None:
How far two readings differ: letter edits divided by the longer reading’s letters, or None when neither has any.




source

flags
def flags(
    text:str, min_chars:int=20
)->list:
List what looks wrong with a page’s text: thin, replacement, legacy, split, akshara or foreign.



test_eq(flags('Hello world this is enough letters'), [])
test_eq(flags('क्ा and more letters here to pass'), ['akshara'])
assert 'split' in flags('कृष्ण\nा is a sign broken off here, long enough')
assert 'legacy' in flags('Jke ‘kfDr ¼ji¼ Hkxoku ¾ ™ more text here')
test_eq(flags(''), ['thin'])
assert disagree('रामः', 'रामा') > 0 and disagree('राम ॥१॥', 'राम') == 0
test_eq(disagree('', ''), None)

title: read
text:
Reading a page
read_page sends one page image to a vision model and returns its blocks, their text joined as markdown (text), the model and the cost its backend reported. With no chat=, the call goes through CachedChat, so each reading is recorded once and replayed after that, and reading the same page again costs nothing. The recordings go in chatcache in the working directory, or the folder $VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE names. A page that has no recording yet reaches the model only when $VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT is set; otherwise read_page raises an error that says so. fresh=True drops the recorded reply and asks the model again. A reply that is not JSON raises an error and is not recorded, so the next try reaches the model. chat= takes any callable in place of a model, which is how the tests run without one, and every image sent is first held to the size limit by fit.
A block keeps its box only when it is four numbers that make a real rectangle, clamped to the page; any other box is dropped. crop cuts a block out of the page image by its box.
Before sending, read_page asks send_rule whether the page may go, as an image. The page’s level is its document’s level, raised to Personal when text, its text layer or OCR, holds an identifier. A page image cannot be masked, so a Personal page goes to a hosted model only with allow=True or pii='off', and a Local only page never does. A page that may not be sent comes back empty, with blocked saying why.


source

read_page
def read_page(
    img:bytes, model:str=None, preset:str='generic', title:str='', script:str='', hint:str='', chat:NoneType=None,
    pii:str='redact', # off|local|redact|refuse; an image cannot be masked, so a Personal page reaches a hosted model only with `allow` or `off`
    level:str='open', # the page's level, from its document; raised to Personal when `text` holds identifiers
    text:str='', # the page's text layer or OCR, to judge it by
    allow:bool=False, # allow once: a Personal page may go to a hosted model; a Local only one never does
    strips:int=1, # sent as this many overlapping strips (`page_strips`), the model told to read the page once

title: read
text:
Reading a document
read_doc(path) takes a PDF or a page image and returns one row per page, {page, text, route, flags}, with blocks, model and cost on a page the model read. route says how the text was got: text (the text layer), ocr, model, or scanned when nothing read the page. pages=[...] limits which pages may go to the model, and the others keep their text layer. Up to workers pages (4) are read at once.
Privacy works page by page, as in read_page. When any page is going to a model, the whole text layer is first checked for a sensitive doctype, so a document whose text reads clearly as a passport or a payslip is Local only before any page image leaves. local_model=, or a built local_chat=, reads the pages that the hosted model may not; without one those pages keep their text layer and carry blocked. A scanned page has no text to check, so it is judged by its document’s level alone.
Long reads need control:

progress(done, total, page, route, cost) is called once with done=0, then after each page that was due for the model. Returning False stops the reading. The pages not yet read keep their text layer or OCR, the result’s cancelled is True and unread lists them. An error raised inside progress is ignored.
cache= keeps each model reading as a JSON file, {page, items, cost, model}, in a folder (p0001.json, or p0001a.json and p0001b.json for the two halves of a spread) or wherever a function cache(page, half) says. A cached page is not sent again: its cost is None, since nothing was spent, and cached is True.
redo=[...] reads those pages again even when cached. Once the new reading is saved, the old one moves to a sibling folder named after the cache folder with _prev added, numbered when an older copy is there already.
spread=True treats a landscape page as two facing pages and reads the halves in turn. strips=k sends each image as k overlapping strips.
clean= is a function applied to each block’s text before it is kept.
tries=n tries a failing page up to n times, waiting RETRY_WAIT seconds (10) after the first failure, 20 after the second, and so on. A page that still fails keeps its text layer, carries its error, and is listed in the result’s failed. Without tries, the first error is raised.

doc_cost(rows) adds up the cost of the pages a model read, and doc_files(folder) lists the PDFs and images under a folder.

title: read
text:
Into the vault
Vault.read_doc(src) reads a file, or every PDF and image under a folder, and adds each file to the vault as one document that search and ask can reach like any other. It also keeps each page in the read_pages table as a version. A page gets a new version only when its text, route or blocks changed, so reading a file twice with the same result adds nothing. Each new version is scanned for personal information and its findings are filed against it (see pii). A new document starts at the shelf’s floor, and one already in the vault at its own level. Vault.pages(doc_id) gives the latest version of each page, and history=True gives every version. Every page read by a hosted model is written to the send log. The result is the ingest result with routes (how many pages took each route), flagged, blocked, cost, model_pages, cancelled, unread and failed added.
Vault.reparse(doc_id, pages=[...]) reads pages of a document again, by default with the model (parse='llm') and with the document’s own preset, script and hint, files the new readings as new versions and re-indexes the document. Use it when a page came out badly and a better model should have it. reparse returns the pages it read, those whose text changed, blocked, cost, model_pages, cancelled and unread. Both methods take progress, and a cancelled reparse leaves its unread pages as they were. When a folder is read with cache=, each file caches in its own subfolder, named after the file.

title: proof
text:
A vision model’s reading of a page is good but not perfect. One way to catch its slips is to have other models, the readers, read the same pages again and compare. Where a reading differs from the stored text, the difference is filed as a change: a run of words to replace, insert or delete, with the names of the readers who made it. Nothing in the document changes until its owner decides.
Vault.proofread(doc_id, readers) has each reader read the pages and files their changes. A change that at least agree readers (2 by default) make identically is proposed, and a change fewer readers make is a doubt. A reader named twice counts once. The owner then works through the review queue:
A change filed against an older version of its page cannot be accepted; accept raises an error that asks for a new proofread. An accept can be undone only while its page has not changed since. edit_change, undo_decision and revert_page are for a person only, and raise PermissionError with by='agent'. proof_md writes the record of a proofread as markdown, page by page: what changed, what is proposed, what is in doubt and what was not taken.

title: proof
text:
Word changes
word_changes(a, b) compares two texts word by word and returns each run of words that b replaces, inserts or deletes, as {at, n, before, after}. at is the index of the first word in a, n is how many of a’s words the change replaces (0 for an insertion), and before and after are the words themselves. apply_changes makes a list of such changes, from the last to the first, and keeps the text’s own spacing and line breaks everywhere else.
A stored page also has blocks, and they have to stay in step with its text. block_changes makes each change in the block its words fall in, and splits a change that crosses the end of a block. A table’s cells and a heading’s ## stay as read. change_box finds the box of the block a change falls in, so a review screen can show the change on the page image.

Proofreading
readers are model ids. chats maps a reader to a stand-in callable, which is how the tests run without models. Each reader reads the page image through read_page, so privacy works as it does there: a reader that may not see a page skips it, and the skip is reported in blocked. A hosted reader may not see a Personal page without allow=True, and no hosted reader sees a Local only page. Each hosted reading is written to the send log.
Running proofread again replaces the open changes, proposed and doubt, on each page it reads, and leaves decided ones alone, so a proofread can be repeated. A change keeps the box of the block it falls in when the page’s blocks have boxes. progress(done, total, page, route, cost) is called once with done=0 and after each page. What was good
rate records one judgement about one section for one question. SIGNALS maps each signal to a label (1 good, 0 bad) and a weight: a thumbs up or down (up, good, down, bad) weighs 3, a section the person read 1.5, a citation 1, and shown, a section that was offered and not cited, counts as a weak negative at 0.35. ratings reads the log back.

title: quality
text:
The Beta prior
doc_prior turns the log into a per-document multiplier on retrieval scores. Each document’s usefulness is modelled as a Beta distribution, updated by its weighted wins and losses, so a document with little evidence stays near neutral and one cited once does not jump ahead. gamma limits how hard the prior may push, and explore is the chance, from 0 to 1, of sampling from the distribution (Thompson sampling) instead of using its mean, which keeps documents with little evidence in play.

    explore:float=1.0, # 1 -> Thompson sample the posterior, 0 -> use its mean
    lo:float=0.6, hi:float=1.6, # clamp, so no amount of evidence can bury a document
    seed:int=None, exclude_ask:NoneType=None, # ignore these questions' rows; for an out-of-fold prior

Noise candidates
suggest_noisy ranks the documents that look most like junk and leaves out any a person has already judged for noise. mark_noisy is the lasting decision: a marked document is left out of search, sections, context and ask. accept_noisy marks the current top suggestions in one call, and mark_noisy_many marks a list.
The features and the Ranker come from litesearch, which computes them from the chunk store alone, and the 0.988 AUC is measured there. The features include how often a chunk turns up among other chunks’ nearest neighbours (hub), how evenly a chunk sits between topics (spread_chunk), how far it is from the middle of the collection (off_centre) and how much of it is duplicated in other documents (dup_out). title: quality
text:
The ranker
The ranker is a pairwise linear model trained on the feedback log: for each question it learns which of two sections should rank higher. fit_ranker(save=True) fits and stores it, and only use_ranker(True), a separate call, puts it in the path of context and so of ask. It is off by default because no learned reranker beat plain reciprocal rank fusion reproducibly in the measurements.

The features
PAIR_FEATURES are signals that are already known when a section is retrieved: its retrieval score and rank, the gap to the top score, the words it shares with the question (raw and weighted by rarity), its cosine similarity to the question, its length, the document prior, the document’s kind and age, and the noise features. The method is in evals/.

title: vishalakshi
text:
vishalakshi keeps what you collect in one SQLite file on your own machine, called a vault, and lets you search it and ask questions of it. One question can draw on a paper, a web page, a talk transcript, your own notes and the source code on disk at once, and the answer cites the sections it used.
It is built from smaller packages. fossick fetches pages, papers and videos. litesearch stores the text and finds it again by keyword and by meaning; a Vault is a litesearch Index, and its search defaults come from there. Urai is the chat interface the vault talks to models through, and Rishi supplies the model backends. kosha indexes source code, and rgapi searches files on disk that nothing has indexed yet. rahasya finds personal information and varga recognises what kind of document something is.

Adding and searching
Vault() with no argument opens ~/.vishalakshi/vault.db. This page uses a throwaway file and fills it with this repository’s own docs and source.

from tempfile import mkdtemp
from litesearch import repo_root
from vishalakshi import Vault

v.enc.note

'minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M (256d, float16, model2vec)'


add takes a directory, a file or a piece of text. grab takes almost anything else, such as an arXiv id, a YouTube link, a GitHub repository, a PDF or a web address, and reads each the right way (acquire). Adding a source that is already in the vault reads it again only when its content changed, and the result’s changed says whether it did. note writes your own note. A note with a key= or a title replaces the earlier note with the same key or title; a note with neither is added as a new one.
Every search result carries age, the seconds since its document was filed, and stale, which is True when the vault believes the document no longer matches its source. Stale results sort last. poll() (below) marks documents stale: a file that changed or vanished, a web page past its time limit that no watch refreshes, or an older copy that a watch has replaced. It deletes only documents that are both stale and replaced.

v.add(root)                       # README.md and every notebook under nbs/

       'prose, kosha embeds identifiers, ripgrep embeds nothing.', tags=['retrieval', 'design'])
v.note('one document per key: writing it again replaces it', title='federation', key='federation')
v.stats()

The default is gemma-4-E2B, a small model that runs on this machine through LiteRT, on the GPU where there is one, and needs no API key. model= names any other model Rishi knows, local or hosted, and chat_kw= passes settings to it. $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL changes the default and $VISHALAKSHI_GPU=0 keeps LiteRT on the CPU. ask retrieves the four best sections (sections=4), shows the model up to 1,500 characters of each (max_chars=1500), and returns the answer with cited, the sections the answer cites (ask).

title: vishalakshi
text:
Personal information and junk
A personal vault holds things that should not leave your machine: invoices, letters, bank statements. vishalakshi looks for personal information in everything it stores, with patterns and checksums rather than a model: email addresses, phone numbers, card and account numbers, national identity numbers, street addresses, dates of birth and API keys. On a held-out test set of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm (evals/RESULTS.md). Names are harder. It finds only names that follow a title such as Dr or Mrs, and only when name detection is on (ner=True); a report’s scanned_ner says whether it looked.
What it finds sets each document’s privacy level: Open, Personal (an identifier was found, or someone marked it), or Local only (set by hand, or a sensitive type such as a passport or a payslip). Each shelf can also have a floor, a level none of its documents goes below. Before every model call the vault decides, with send_check, what each document may give a hosted model, meaning one that runs anywhere but this machine: an Open document goes whole, a Personal one masked or not at all, a Local only one never. A document’s title, headings and source path go under the same rule as its text. A model on this machine may read everything. Each send to a hosted model is recorded in the vault’s send log. The details are on pii.
Junk is a separate problem: cookie banners and site footers that match every search and answer nothing. suggest_noisy ranks likely junk without any labels (0.988 AUC on the test corpora) and mark_noisy takes a document out of search (quality).

from vishalakshi.pii import pii_report

r = pii_report('Invoice for ada@example.com. Card 4111 1111 1111 1111. KEY=sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456')
r.has_pii, r.identifying, r.kinds

      title='footer', source='/inbox/footer.md')

pii= in ask
what happens when the retrieved sections hold personal information




local
a model on this machine answers, told never to repeat a personal detail; if the model is not local, nothing is sent


redact
each recognised identifier is masked, then the named model answers, hosted or not. The heading, title and source of each section are masked with its text. Names without a title are not masked


refuse
no model is asked, and the result says what was held back



The default is local when a local runtime is installed and redact when not. ask cannot run with detection off: pii='off' warns and applies the default. The result’s policy says which was used, and any identifier the model repeats is masked in the answer. Under every policy a hosted model gets a Local only section only as a placeholder, with no heading, title or source. Search and reading take pii= too (off, redact or refuse), and there the default is off, which returns the stored text. The MCP server defaults to redact for every tool and refuses off, since its client is a model the vault does not run.

text:
Watches and the queue
A watch repeats an acquisition on a schedule. Its action is an acquisition method (url, web, harvest, arxiv, youtube, crawl or path), remind to write a note, or folder; kind= is the same thing under another name. A folder watch keeps a snapshot of a directory and fires with what was added, changed or removed, together with its instructions for whoever reviews the change. A schedule is every='6h' or cron='0 9 * * 1', and pobblebonk keeps the schedules in the vault file.
poll() is the tick to call from cron or an app’s timer. It returns jobs whose worker died to the queue, queues the watches that are due, runs the queue, and every ten minutes runs housekeep. A failed fetch is retried with a growing delay and set aside as dead after five attempts; jobs(state='dead') lists those. See jobs.

v.watch('https://example.com/changelog', action='url', every='6h')
v.watch('late chunking retrieval', action='web', every='1d', n=5)
v.watch('Re-read the evals', action='remind', every='1w')
v.watch(Path(root)/'nbs', kind='folder', every='1h', instructions='flag any print() left in a notebook', pattern='*.ipynb')
L(v.watches()).map(lambda w: (w['kind'], w['target'][:34], w['every'], w['pattern']))

title: vishalakshi
text:
Books and scans
A scanned book has no usable text layer, and an old print set in a legacy font may have one that reads as gibberish. read_doc reads a PDF or a page image page by page and picks a route for each page (parse='auto'): a text layer that passes its checks is kept, a scanned page is OCRed, and a page still scanned or flagged as garbled goes to a vision model, local or hosted. preset= picks the reading prompt (generic, sanskrit, tamil or tables), and hint= adds a sentence about the book. Given a folder, it reads every PDF and image under it. Each page’s text, route and flags are kept as numbered versions, so reading a page again with a better model (reparse) never loses the earlier reading. A page image cannot be masked, so a Personal page goes to a hosted model only with allow=True, and a Local only page never does. Readings are recorded and replayed through CachedChat, and a page with no recording yet reaches the model only when $VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT is set or a chat= is passed (read).
proofread has other models read the pages again and files the word changes each reading would make. A change two readers agree on is proposed, and one that only one reader makes is in doubt. Nothing changes until the owner decides: accept applies changes as a new version of the page, reject sets them aside, and undo_decision and revert_page take decisions back (proof).

v.read_doc('books/', parse='auto', model='claude/sonnet', preset='sanskrit', hint='verses end in ॥ n ॥')
doc = v.read_doc('scan.pdf', parse='llm', model='gemini/gemini-2.5-flash')['doc_id']
v.pages(doc)                                   # text, route (text, ocr, model, proof), flags, version
v.reparse(doc, pages=[3, 4], model='claude/opus')
v.proofread(doc, ['claude/sonnet', 'gemini/gemini-2.5-pro'])
v.changes(doc, 'proposed'); v.accept(doc); print(v.proof_md(doc))
read_doc('scan.pdf', parse='auto', model='claude/sonnet')   # no vault: the pages alone

title: code
text:
Source code is a poor fit for an index built for prose: the useful units are functions and classes, the useful names are identifiers, and what matters is who calls what. kosha is the vault’s code index. It splits source files into functions and classes using their syntax tree, embeds them with a model trained on code, and builds a call graph in which each symbol has a PageRank score, a measure of how central it is. kosha keeps its index in .kosha/ inside the repository, not in the vault file.
index_code(dir) builds or updates that index; afterwards only changed files are indexed again. code_search searches it. symbol(name) gives one function or class with its file, PageRank, callers and callees, and where_to_add(description) ranks the places in the repository where a described change belongs.
source

def index_code(
    dir:str=None, # repo to index
    graph:bool=True, # also build the AST call graph (callers, callees, PageRank)
    env:bool=False, # also index installed packages (slow the first time)
    force:bool=False, # reindex everything, graph included, rather than what changed
    verbose:bool=False, **kw
)->dict: # forwarded to kosha's `sync`
Build or update kosha’s index of a repository, and return its status.
source

def kosha(
    dir:str=None, # repo root; defaults to the cwd repo
    share_encoder:bool=False, # embed code with the vault's encoder instead of kosha's
    **kw

The kosha index for the repository dir, kept on the vault so every code method uses the same one.
grep(pattern) runs ripgrep, through rgapi, over the files on disk. It finds exact text, including in files kosha never indexed or that changed since the last index_code, and it respects .gitignore.

title: jobs
text:
Fetching a page, ingesting a batch of files or rebuilding the topic map can fail or be interrupted. Queue keeps such work as rows in a jobs table in the vault’s own SQLite file, so a job outlives the process that queued it, and no separate server is needed. enqueue adds a job. A worker takes jobs with claim, which marks them as running and gives the worker a lease: a time limit (lease, 10 minutes) on its claim. Two workers claiming at once never get the same job. If a worker dies, its lease runs out and reclaim puts the job back. A job that fails is retried after a delay that doubles each time, from 30 seconds up to 6 hours, and after max_attempts (5) failures it becomes dead: it stays in the table, with its error, for a person to look at.
Because the queue lives in the same file as the documents, a job queued inside a write_txn is committed together with the write that caused it. Queue needs only a database and knows nothing about a vault; acquire registers the vault’s own jobs on it.

title: jobs
text:
The queue
A job has a kind, which names the handler that runs it, and a payload, a dict stored as JSON. key makes queueing idempotent: while a job with the same kind and key is still waiting or running, enqueueing it again returns that job instead of adding a second one, so re-running the same fan-out does not double the work. Lower priority runs first.


source

Queue
def Queue(
    db, # open litesearch/fastlite Database; the queue lives in its file
    lease:float=600, # seconds a claim is held before another worker may take the job
    max_attempts:int=5, # attempts before a job is dead-lettered
    base:float=30, # first retry delay; doubles per attempt
    keep:float=604800, # how long finished jobs and run history survive `purge`, 7d
    busy_ms:int=30000, # lock wait before a write gives up; apsw's stock default is 100ms
):
A job queue stored in an open litesearch database, which runs every job at least once.




source

Queue.enqueue_all
def enqueue_all(
    kind:str, payloads, **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Enqueue many jobs of one kind in a single transaction.




source

Queue.enqueue
def enqueue(
    kind:str, # which handler runs it
    payload:dict=None, # arguments, stored as JSON
    run_at:float=None, # epoch seconds; defaults to now
    priority:int=0, # lower runs first
    key:str=None, # idempotency key: an identical key still ready or running wins
    max_attempts:int=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Add one job, or return the waiting or running job that already has this key.



Claiming
claim picks and marks its jobs in a single SQL statement, and SQLite lets only one write run at a time, so another worker cannot slip in between the pick and the mark. What a worker gets back is already running and already leased.
ack (finished) and fail (failed) only count while the caller still holds the lease. A handler slower than lease has its job reclaimed and given to another worker. Without this check its late ack could mark as done a job another worker is still running, or its fail could send a finished job back for a third run. Instead the late call comes back lost, and the run history says so.


source

Queue.reclaim
def reclaim(
    now:float=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Put jobs whose lease expired back on the queue, so a worker that died loses its claim but not the job.




source

Queue.fail
def fail(
    job, # the claimed job
    error:str, # what went wrong; truncated to 500 chars on the row
    after:float=None, # seconds until the retry; None uses `backoff`
    dead:bool=False, # dead-letter now, whatever the attempts left: retrying a 401 never turns into success
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Record a failure and schedule a retry after the backoff delay, or mark the job dead once its attempts are spent.




source

Queue.ack
def ack(
    job
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Mark a claimed job done, or return it as lost when this worker’s lease was reclaimed.




source

Queue.claim
def claim(
    worker:str='worker', # who is holding the lease; recorded on the row and in history
    n:int=1, # how many jobs to take
    now:float=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Claim up to n due jobs in one statement; no job was claimed twice over 400 jobs and 8 processes (evals/jobs.py).




Running
A handler is a function fn(payload), registered with register or the on decorator. run_one runs one claimed job, and drain claims and runs until the queue is empty or limit jobs have run; it is what a cron job calls. How a handler ends decides what happens next:

Terminal is for failures that waiting cannot fix: a 401, a model name that does not exist, a file that is gone. With the default schedule a doomed job would otherwise be retried for most of a day. A job whose kind has no handler is dead at once for the same reason.

    limit:int=1000, # jobs to run before returning; a ceiling, not a target

Claim and run jobs until the queue is empty or limit jobs have run.

Looking at it
jobs lists jobs by state and kind, pending counts what is left, stats counts each state, and history lists past runs. Dead jobs are the queue’s inbox for a person: dead lists them with the error that finished them off, and since nothing is deleted on failure, retry simply puts one back with its attempt count reset. purge deletes finished jobs and run history older than keep (7 days) and leaves dead jobs alone.

title: mcp
text:
MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is how AI assistants and editors call outside tools. vishalakshi-mcp is an MCP server that offers vault methods as tools. TOOLS lists them. Each tool is built with the same cmd the command line uses, so its arguments and description are the method’s own. The server’s instructions tell a model which tool to reach for first: context before answering a question, grab to file something, note to write a conclusion back.
An MCP client is treated as an agent, never as a person: every tool that takes by is called with by='agent', and by is not offered. So a client can raise a privacy level or mark a document personal, but it cannot clear a mark, reject a finding or lower a level (see pii).
For the same reason every result passes through client_view before the client sees it, since the client is a model the vault does not run. Each string under a Local only document is withheld, title, heading and source included, and every other string goes through redact, so a Personal document’s identifiers are masked. A document a person cleared with mark_not_pii comes back as stored. A tool that takes pii defaults to redact here, where the CLI defaults to off. A client may ask for refuse, which withholds more. It may not ask for off: as with lowering a level, only a person can turn the gate off. ask returns no prompt, and when a local model read a Local only section whole, its answer is withheld too. To use the server, add it to the client’s configuration:
The server talks over standard input and output by default; vishalakshi-mcp --http serves Streamable HTTP instead.

Models and backends
A model is named by an id, and Rishi works out which backend runs it: LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp or Ollama on this machine, or a hosted API, which needs its API key. LiteRT is the default local path. title: concepts
text:
Encoders
An encoder, or embedding model, turns text into vectors so that texts with similar meanings land near each other. The default is a static multilingual model producing 256 numbers per text, stored as 16-bit floats. offline=True hashes character sequences instead, which needs no download but matches spelling rather than meaning. A shelf records the encoder that wrote it.

Vault(':memory:', offline=True).enc.note      # never attempt a download; also the CI default

'char-n-gram hashing (256d): lexical only; pass encoder= or restore network access for real semantics'



Vault(encoder='minishlab/potion-science-32M')   # pick a different one

Vault('/Users/71293/.vishalakshi/vault.db': 0 docs, 0 chunks, 0 entities, encoder=model2vec)


16-bit floats are litesearch’s default width. One vector index holds one encoder’s vectors, so documents embedded by different encoders need different shelves.
ENCODERS holds three aliases, each a plain model id: multilingual, the default; code, the model kosha uses for identifiers; and gemma, the slowest and most faithful. Any other model2vec id works by name too.

from vishalakshi.core import ENCODERS

ENCODERS

A static model is a lookup table from words to vectors, so it embeds a document in milliseconds without a GPU. litesearch measured weighted MRR between 0.018 and 0.046 across four encoders, which is why the static default is the chosen trade-off (evals/encoder.py). gemma is an ONNX model, and choosing it is what loads onnxruntime.

# `encoder=` also takes any object with an `.encode`, which is what a shelf gets when you build one
import numpy as np
from vishalakshi.core import mk_encoder

class Eight:
    def encode(self, xs, **kw): return np.zeros((len(xs), 8), dtype=np.float16)

e = mk_encoder(Eight())
e.dims, e.method, e.name

One vector index is one vector space, so different encoders need different shelves. SHELVES names the shelves the vault uses itself, and KIND_SHELF says which kinds acquisition sends to their own shelf.

from vishalakshi.core import SHELVES, KIND_SHELF

SHELVES, KIND_SHELF


papers = v.shelf('papers')        # reuses the live encoder unless a registry entry exists
papers.add('# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.', 'a paper')

[(s['store'], s['encoder'], s['docs']) for s in v.shelves()]

KIND_SHELF routes documents as they arrive. reshelf moves a document later, once its doctype is known, and elsewhere searches the other shelves.

v.route('arxiv').name, v.route('web').name

('papers', 'store')


A PDF may be an invoice or a paper, and its kind cannot tell which. categorize decides after the document is filed, and reshelf moves it to the shelf its doctype belongs on.

v.add('# Attention is all you need\n\n## Abstract\n\nWe propose the Transformer.\n\n'
      '## Introduction\n\nRelated work [1] et al.\n\n## References\n\ndoi:10.1/x',
      'attention', source='/inbox/attention.pdf')

r = v.reshelf('/inbox/attention.pdf', llm='never')
r.doctype, r.was, r.store, r.moved

('paper', 'store', 'papers', True)



v.doc('/inbox/attention.pdf'), v.shelf('papers').doc('/inbox/attention.pdf')['title']

(None, 'attention')


Moving a document adds it to the new shelf from scratch, so its vectors are made again by that shelf’s encoder, and the copy on the old shelf is deleted. Its meta goes with it, with the doctype and the shelf it came from. Marks are keyed to a document on its shelf, so they do not move with it.
federate treats each shelf as one more search to merge by rank, beside kosha and ripgrep. elsewhere adds a couple of sections from the neighbouring shelves to context and ask.

v.federate('contextual chunk embeddings', repo=False, grep=False).legs

{'prose': 3, 'shelf:papers': 4}


Each row from elsewhere names the shelf it came from in store. Pass that to read(node_id, store=...) when the section is not on the current shelf.

e = v.elsewhere('contextual chunk embeddings')
L(e).map(lambda r: (r.store, r.breadcrumb))

v.read(e[0].node_id, store=e[0].store)['text'][:80]

'# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.'


A shelf records the encoder that wrote it and reopens with the same one. Opening it with a different encoder raises an error rather than mixing two vector spaces. To change a shelf’s encoder on purpose, drop the shelf and add its documents again.

section: Deciding what a model may be sent
text:
Deciding what a model may be sent
send_check decides, before anything goes to a model, how each document, page or piece of text goes: whole, masked, or not at all (withheld). It returns the decisions in rows, the subsets send, masked and withheld, and a why sentence for a person to read before sending, for example gpt-4.1-nano, hosted. 1 personal document masked, 1 document open, 1 local-only document withheld. The rule itself is send_rule:

A model on this machine gets everything whole. model_local decides what counts as local: LiteRT, MLX and llama.cpp always, Ollama only when $OLLAMA_HOST points at this machine. Anything else, including a chat that names no runtime, is hosted.
An Open item goes whole to any model.
A Local only item is withheld from a hosted model under every policy, even with allow=True.
A Personal item goes to a hosted model masked under redact, and is withheld under local and refuse. A page image cannot be masked, so a Personal page image is withheld under every policy except off.
allow=True, allow once, sends Personal items whole for that one call, as policy='off' does.

ask, explain, categorize, extract, read_doc, reparse and proofread all decide through this rule. The decision covers everything that goes with the text: a document’s title, its headings and its source path are masked with it or withheld with it. A page image is read with the document’s title in its prompt, so the title is judged with the page. build_graph, and connect through it, sends every chunk to its chat with nothing to mask, so a hosted chat builds the graph only when every document on the shelf is Open; otherwise nothing is sent and the result says why. Masking replaces only what the detector recognises. A document marked Personal by hand, with nothing recognisable in it, therefore goes to a hosted model under redact exactly as it is stored.
Each send to a hosted model is recorded in the vault’s send_log table: when, which document and pages, which model and runtime, the policy, and the kinds of personal information where they are known. sends(ref) reads it back, newest first. Sends to a local model are not logged, and withheld items are not in the log.

Recording what a model said
CachedChat records a model’s replies on disk and plays them back, so tests and these pages can show real answers without running the model again. Give it a folder of recordings and the vault treats it as any other chat. The folder is path, else $VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE, else chatcache in the working directory. title: ask
section: When the sections hold personal information
text:
When the sections hold personal information
The detector and the marks are explained on pii. The cells below show what ask does with them. They use a stand-in chat that records what it was sent, so a leak would show up as a recorded call.
The check runs on the chat that was built, before anything is sent. Here a hosted chat is lent under the default local policy, so the model is never called.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'THIS MUST NEVER BE SENT'))
test_eq(_seen, {})                       # the model was never called at all
test_eq(r.refused, True)
r.answer

'held back: these sections hold personal information (card, email, phone) and remote is not a local runtime, so nothing was sent to it'


With a local runtime the private sections go to the local model under PII_SP, which tells it to answer with counts, kinds and totals instead of personal details, and to say what it held back.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('litert',
    'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. '
    'Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'))
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'litert')
test_eq(_seen['sp'], PII_SP)             # not VAULT_SP: that one tells it to cite, and a citation points at the text
test_eq(r.get('refused', False), False)
r.answer

'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'


instruction= sends a follow-up turn. When the local model holds something back it says which instruction would let it answer, such as “give me the total and the due date”, and the caller sends that instruction with the same question.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', instruction='Give me the total and the due date only.',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'))
test_eq('Instruction from the questioner' in _seen['prompt'], True)
r.answer

'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'


Every answer over private sections is scanned again before it is returned. Identifiers the model repeated anyway are masked, and leaked lists their kinds.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'It is for ada@example.com, card 4111 1111 1111 1111.'))
test_eq(r.answer, 'It is for [EMAIL], card [CARD].')
r.leaked

{'email': 1, 'card': 1}


pii='redact' masks the recognised identifiers in each section’s text, then lets a hosted model answer. A name is masked only when a title such as Dr comes before it, so “Ada Lovelace” goes through, as a real-model cell further down shows.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', pii='redact', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'))
test_eq('ada@example.com' in _seen['prompt'], False)
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'remote')
r.answer

'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'


A structured answer (schema=) has its fields scrubbed the same way. An API key counts as personal information, so a hosted chat is refused for it just as for an email address, and so is a document that was marked by hand.

title: extract
text:
Search finds documents; this page is about what is in them. A doctype is the kind of document: an invoice, a receipt, a contract, a paper, meeting notes, a passport, and 31 types in all. It is separate from a document’s kind, which records how the document arrived (web, pdf, note and so on). The doctype decides which schema extract uses, that is which fields it asks a model for (an invoice has a number, a vendor, a total and line items), and which shelf reshelf moves the document to.
varga holds the cue table that recognises each doctype, the schemas, and the code that makes a model answer in a schema’s shape. This page stores varga’s verdicts in the vault and runs extraction through the vault’s model and its privacy checks.
categorize decides a document’s doctype and writes it into the document’s meta. It first scores the document against varga’s cue table: phrases such as “invoice no” or “total due”, amounts of money, dates, organisation names. score is the winning type’s score and decisive says whether it beat the runner-up clearly. Only when the cues are not decisive does it ask a model. With llm='auto', the default, a local model is asked only if it is already downloaded, so categorising never starts a download; llm='always' asks a model every time and llm='never' never does. The model gets the document’s title and its text through send_check, so a private document’s title and text reach a hosted model masked or not at all. A file read off disk is judged on its name as well as its text. by says how the verdict was reached.
A verdict the cues reached decisively, or one a model gave, is written as doctype. An undecided one that scores at least REVIEW_SCORE (0.2) is only proposed, in doctype_proposed, for a person to confirm: proposed_types lists the proposals, surest first, and accept_type, accept_types and reject_type settle them. This is the same two-step review that suggest_noisy and accept_noisy use for noise. Below 0.2 nothing is written, and reshelf never moves a document on a proposal. categorize_all types every untyped document on the shelf.

title: extract
text:
Extraction
extract reads a whole document, up to max_chars, and returns its fields as a dict. Without a schema it categorises the document first and takes its doctype’s schema: an invoice gets Invoice, and a doctype with no schema of its own gets Summary. A schema can also be a SCHEMAS key, a dataclass, or a string such as 'vendor:str, total:float'. The model is made to answer in the schema’s shape with a tool call, a grammar or parsed JSON, whichever its backend supports. check=True reads every value back through check_fields and lists what did not fit in errors. src gives the page and block each field was read from, and cite=True adds the quote. extract_all(doctype='invoice') runs over every invoice and returns one row per document.
Privacy works as in ask, with pii='local' as the default here. The decision is send_check’s. A private document is read by the local pii_model or by nothing, redact masks its title, source and text for a hosted model, and refuse reads nothing. A Local only document goes to no hosted model under any policy, off included. A model on this machine reads the document whole. Each hosted send is written to the send log. Fields read from a private document are scanned and masked before they are returned or saved.

title: core
text:
A vault is one SQLite file that holds everything you have collected, such as web pages, papers, talk transcripts, PDFs, notes and source files, all searchable together. Vault() opens ~/.vishalakshi/vault.db, Vault(path) opens or creates any other file, and Vault(':memory:') makes one that lasts only as long as the process.
A Vault is a litesearch Index, and litesearch decides how text is stored and found. Each thing you add becomes a document. A document is split along its headings into a tree of sections, which litesearch calls nodes, and each section’s text is cut into chunks. Every chunk is stored twice: as text, for SQLite’s full-text keyword search, and as a vector, a list of numbers from an embedding model that puts texts with similar meanings near each other. A search runs both and merges the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), which scores each chunk by its rank in each list rather than by the raw scores, because a keyword score and a vector distance cannot be compared. The default embedding model is potion-multilingual-128M, which is small, fast and covers over 100 languages, Devanagari among them; encoder= picks another (see concepts).
The vault adds to that a kind on every document, saying how it arrived (web, pdf, arxiv, note, code and so on), shelves that keep separate collections in the same file, marks that record a person’s judgements about a document, an entity graph and topic map, and the methods on the other pages that fetch, read, extract and answer.

A shelf opened from a vault shares the vault’s embedding model in memory, so opening many shelves loads the model once. offline=True, or $VISHALAKSHI_OFFLINE, carries over to a new shelf as well, so an offline vault never downloads a model.

# A shelf is a partition, not a second encoder, so it reuses the vault's live one.
from tempfile import mkdtemp

v = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'v.db')
s = v.shelf('project')

# a shelf with no registry row used to fall through to the default and load a real model
o = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'o.db', offline=True)
assert o.enc.method == 'hash' and o.shelf('fresh').enc.method == 'hash'
